page: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include a GPU. Network connectivity is rated at a 4 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in specific areas, notably in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 188.91 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.22 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core execution at 1883.0. Text processing also registers a strong score of 2344.0. Conversely, the instance exhibits weaknesses in cryptographic operations, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1509.87. Large language model inference capabilities are limited, as demonstrated by a poor prompt processing speed of 15.58 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, though text generation on the same model averages 11.4 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8g.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for arm64-native workloads, providing dedicated physical cores without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is suited for compute-bound tasks that benefit from high single-core performance and strong memory read bandwidth, such as text processing, software compilation, and lightweight web serving. However, workloads requiring hardware-accelerated cryptography or large-scale LLM inference may encounter performance bottlenecks.
